# A short, source-linked reading of the case

**Editorial notes prepared with AI assistance, not generated by the rule extractor and not human peer reviewed.** These notes illustrate what a researcher can assemble after opening the evidence. They are separate from the unedited [automatic draft](outputs/draft.md).

## What can be compared?

| Paper | Problem addressed | Reported approach | Boundary for interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zaffran et al. (2023), PDF p. 1 | Missing covariates; marginal coverage can conceal differences between missingness patterns | Missing-data augmentation within conformalized quantile regression | Regression and missingness-pattern guarantees; inspect the assumptions in the paper before transferring the guarantee |
| Ghosh et al. (2023), PDF p. 1 | Prediction-set robustness to input perturbations | Adaptive probabilistically robust conformal prediction, with thresholds for samples and perturbations | Classification; coverage over most perturbations is different from a worst-case guarantee |
| Cruz Cabezas et al. (2025), PDF pp. 1–2 | Narrow predictions in sparsely observed regions | EPICSCORE introduces epistemic uncertainty into conformal scores | Marginal finite-sample and asymptotic conditional statements have different scopes; this is not a guarantee of reliability everywhere |

Read the three [publisher sources](README.md#selection-attribution-and-license) and the [saved pages](outputs/run.json) alongside this table. Page numbers refer to the PDF file, not the proceedings' page numbering.

## Draft review paragraph

These three papers address different ways in which a useful prediction set can fail to reflect the information available to the model. Zaffran et al. focus on missing covariates and motivate attention to coverage conditional on missingness patterns (PDF p. 1). Ghosh et al. study robustness of classification prediction sets under input perturbations, introducing a probabilistic robustness target (PDF p. 1). Cruz Cabezas et al. instead modify conformal scores to account for epistemic uncertainty, including regions with little training data (PDF pp. 1–2). Their guarantees concern different conditions and tasks. The present corpus therefore supports a comparison of problem formulations and assumptions, **not a common numerical leaderboard or a claim that one method dominates the others**.

## What is still missing?

This example does not harmonize datasets, reimplement methods, test assumptions or reproduce reported experiments. The Ghosh supplement is outside the imported corpus. The automatic extractor misses relevant sentences and includes bibliographic fragments: see the [audit](audit.md). A publishable synthesis would need a broader search, explicit eligibility criteria and direct checking of theorem conditions and empirical comparisons. These are outstanding research tasks, not results supplied by this demonstration.
